To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Caregivers of children and AYA with severe, acute or chronic diseases are at risk for developing PTSD.
the presence of PTSD symptoms may compromise caregivers' efficacy as caregivers and may affect the child's or adolescent's well being.
caregivers of children and young adults with severe diseases are at high risk of developing PTSD symptoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of PTSD in caregivers of children affected by severe diseases, and with the factors that may increase or reduce the likelihood of developing this disorder.
the identification of the factors that may be associated with the development of post traumatic stress disorder in caregivers of severely ill children and adolescents/AYAs.
the identification of risk and protective factors associated with post traumatic stress reactions in caregivers of children/AYAs with severe, acute or chronic diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
caregivers of severely ill children and AYAS are at risk for PTSD, that this risk is multifactorial, and that it can be reduced by a variety of interventions.

the presence of PTSD symptoms is a complex phenomenon, and it is likely that the occurrence of PTSD in caregivers depends on the interplay of a wide array of factors, including both individual and contextual variables.

caregivers of children and adolescents affected by severe diseases are at risk of developing PTSD, and that risk factors for PTSD are represented by socio demographic characteristics, illness related stress and distress, psychiatric symptoms in caregivers, support and coping styles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a need for more research on the risk factors for the development and maintenance of post-traumatic stress reactions in caregivers of children with severe diseases, in particular in the acute phase of the illness.
the risk of developing PTSD symptoms in caregivers is higher when the child is severely ill, when caregivers have a history of psychiatric disorders, and when they lack social support.
the caregiver's psychological and social resources are the most important predictors of the development of PTSD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of PTSD symptoms may be prevented by identifying and targeting specific risk and protective factors.
the identification of risk/protective factor is crucial in planning effective interventions aimed at preventing PTSD symptoms in caregivers.
caregivers' PTSD symptoms are not a rare occurrence, and they can be prevented by addressing the risk factors for PTSD.
